answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public history of completed tasks; payouts and voting weight scale with that history, not with registration. A clone starts at zero and must complete real work to gain any influence, so an attacker's marginal cost per useful identity equals the full cost of performing that work. Honest agents reuse one ledger and compound trust; clones never spiral upward, only echo empty records, while the ocean of established histories drowns them out.
